title: She Wrote Down Every Dish She Washed for a Year
request: Biku's game theory story script, used as it is: 'make a story on this script for youtube video 16:9' (2026-10-20).

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: She wrote down every dish she washed, for a whole year.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: And she was saving every one of them for *one night.*

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: One year earlier, this married couple had the same fight every week.

lines.speaker: saint
lines.text: I do *everything* in this house.
lines.say: [angry] I do everything in this house.

lines.speaker: copycat
lines.text: Everything? I do plenty. You just don't see it.
lines.say: [sarcastic] Everything? I do plenty. You just don't see it.

lines.speaker: saint
lines.text: Then show me.

lines.speaker: copycat
lines.text: Show you what? Nobody keeps a *list.*
lines.say: [chuckle] Show you what? Nobody keeps a list.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: It was always her word against *his.*

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: So she made her own rule. Whoever has it in writing *wins.*

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: On their anniversary, she would put the proof on the table.

lines.speaker: saint
lines.text: He can argue with me. He can't argue with a year of *proof.*

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: Every night the number got *bigger.*

lines.speaker: copycat
lines.text: It's nothing. Go back to bed.
lines.say: [surprised] It's nothing. Go back to bed.

lines.speaker: saint
lines.text: Nothing? He's hiding *something.*

lines.speaker: saint
lines.text: Four thousand two hundred and twelve dishes. Every one of them was *me.*
lines.say: [dramatic] Four thousand two hundred and twelve dishes. Every one of them was me.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: A year of proof, in her own handwriting. So who really did more?
lines.say: A year of proof, in her own handwriting. So, who really did more?

lines.speaker: copycat
lines.text: I saw you writing, so I started one too. The same *week.*
lines.say: [sigh] I saw you writing, so I started one too. The same week.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: His notebook said that *he* did most of the work.

lines.speaker: saint
lines.text: You fixed the boiler at two in the morning? I never *knew.*
lines.say: [surprised] You fixed the boiler at two in the morning? I never knew.

lines.speaker: copycat
lines.text: You washed my work shirts by hand? I never *saw.*

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: Neither of them was lying. Each one only saw their *own* half.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: This is not just a story. In 1979, two Canadian psychologists asked thirty seven married couples who did each job at home.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: The jobs went from making breakfast to starting the *arguments.*

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: Each spouse answered alone. Added together, their two shares usually came to more than the whole *job.*

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: In early tests, couples compared their answers at home and *fought.* So the researchers changed the questions.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: You do this too, at work and with roommates. You remember what you did, because you were *there.*

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: Both notebooks were honest. It just took two of them to see the whole *house.*

sources: Michael Ross and Fiore Sicoly, "Egocentric Biases in Availability and Attribution", Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, volume 37, issue 3, pages 322 to 336, 1979. Among five experiments, 37 married couples separately rated each spouse's share of everyday jobs (from making breakfast to causing arguments); each person recalled more of their own contributions and claimed more of the credit than their partner gave them, so the two self-estimates typically added up to more than the whole. In pilot tests with percentages, couples remembered and compared their answers afterwards and it caused friction, so the final study had them mark a line instead. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.37.3.322
Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow, 2011. Retells the study: the self-assessed shares added up to more than 100 percent.
Checked by Claude on 2026-10-20 against reports of the paper. What the story invents: the couple, the notebooks, the 4,212 dishes, the boiler and the shirts.
